live.spec_caveat: 3×3-pixel sum minus the median of a ring 3–5 pixels out, converted with each picture's pixel solid angle. Error bars come from the ring's scatter and ignore the correlated noise added by resampling. Colours: earlier and later pictures, split at the largest gap in time.
live.changes_method: A change is a group of at least 2 pixels deviating by more than 5σ from the expected value, with a noise floor of {f} × the source brightness. Single-pixel spikes are removed with a 3 × 3 median filter.

start.f1_line: Most of what a plain blink flags comes from comparing pictures from different detectors, which differ in colour and in sharpness.
view.det_what: SPHEREx has six detectors, and each covers one band of infrared colour. A linear variable filter makes the wavelength change across each detector, so the same star is seen at a different wavelength within the band on each visit.
reveal.own_noise: noise from its own error estimate
reveal.evidence: The {N} pictures and the empty-path tests behind these numbers
home.intro: Epoch shows every picture NASA's SPHEREx telescope has taken of a patch of sky, in time order. SPHEREx takes each picture in a different infrared colour, so a plain blink between pictures shows changes even where nothing changed. Watching one detector at a time removes most of those false changes.
home.patch_line: On this patch: {all} changes in the plain blink, {det} when each detector is viewed on its own (all six added up); that is {pct}% removed.
home.patch_median: The {hl} figure is the median over {n} other, randomly chosen patches.
tm.f1_line: Every picture is taken in a different infrared colour, so a plain blink flags changes even when nothing moved. Watching one detector at a time removes most of them; some of the removed changes are real, and neither view catches faint moving asteroids in single pictures. Across our random test patches:
live.note_snapped: The position you typed is on the path {name} has travelled since 2000, so we centred on where it is now.
live.note_exact: Show exactly the position I typed
live.gaia_legend: Green circles: Gaia DR3 stars, moved to the date of each picture (the {max} brightest around this patch at most, from {service}; a bigger circle is a brighter star). An arrow shows {yr} years of motion for stars faster than {pm}″ per year. Click a circle for its Gaia number, brightness and motion. A source with no circle is not in Gaia: WISE 0855, for example, is too cold and faint for it. A circle with no source is a star too faint for SPHEREx.

live.track_wait: This view appears once all pictures are in.
live.track_hint: Each picture is moved back along the motion you set to where the object would have been at the reference time, so something moving that way piles up into one dot while whatever is left of the still sky smears out (the pictures used are the colour-aware ones, with the still sky removed detector by detector).
live.track_info: Reference time {date} UTC (MJD {mjd}) · {n} pictures within the span ({N} loaded), taken over {h} hours · {nc} of them still cover the centre after shifting · over that time the motion set carries an object {d}″ ({px} pixels).
live.track_few: Fewer than two pictures in this span: widen it or move the reference time.
live.track_plain: Plain stack: pictures added as they are
live.track_follow: Followed stack: each picture shifted back along the motion
live.track_peak: Brightest point within {r} pixels ({as}″) of the centre: {a} × noise in the plain stack, {b} × noise in the followed stack.
live.track_scale: Colour: orange is brighter than the still sky, blue is fainter; full colour at ±{clip} times each stack's own noise (its robust scatter). Each picture's values are capped at ±{clip} before adding, so one spike cannot dominate. Dashed pink line on the plain stack: the path the motion set would trace. Yellow ticks: the centre.
live.track_example_post: (V {V}; speed, direction and time from its catalogue orbit, and the view is centred where the orbit puts it at the reference time).
live.track_mark_h: Don't know the motion? Mark the object in two pictures
live.track_mark_hint: Press “Mark start”, pick a picture with the slider and click the object; then pick a later picture and click it again. Speed and direction are worked out from the two pictures' times.
live.track_mark_done: From your two marks: {rate}″ per hour towards {pa}° east of north.
live.track_mark_same: Both marks are on pictures taken at the same time; pick pictures taken at different times.
live.track_pick_aria: One picture from the span, still sky removed. Click the object to mark it.
live.track_smooth: Smooth each stack to the blur size (3 × 3 pixels; helps faint point sources)
live.track_faint: (V {V}), one of the faint asteroids in our results that only shows up when all its pictures are combined along its orbit, does not stand out in this quick view.
live.track_try: Moving objects: the “Follow a mover” view adds pictures along a motion you choose.
results.rule: Each test and its pass criterion were defined before the analysis. Post hoc checks are marked as such.
results.legend: Verdicts are taken from the project's claims ledger; each claim has an identifier such as C17. Supported: the predefined criterion was met. Not confirmed: measured, but below the predefined threshold. Failed: the criterion was not met or the method did not work. All values are read from the result files.
